newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil-Weather problems to push up prices.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil-Weather problems to push up prices.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to be firm this week because intermittent rains in coconut growing areas in the past several days has delayed copra deliveries to the mills, Manila vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
"I expect the domestic market to lead the way. Copra in the local market now is in fact higher than export values," said a trader with one of Philippine's largest coconut oil millers.
Traders said Manila buyers of copra quoted 14 pesos per kg early today. A kg of the commodity fetched an average of 13 pesos at the start of the year, one trader said.

"With copra prices more expensive in the local market than export values, expect less origin sellers from the Philippines for the export markets this week," the trader in the Philippine coconut oil mill said.
Philippine vegetable oil traders said copra deliveries from the farms to the oil mills have slowed down in the past several days due to weather problems.

"I don't expect Indonesia to fill up the supply gap that will manifest shortly because of reports of weather problems in coconut growing areas in Indonesia also in the past several days," the trader said.
Coconut oil stocks in Rotterdam as of February 10 dipped to 28,886 tonnes from 30,913 tonnes on February 3.
Traders said they expect coconut oil supplies in Rotterdam to go down further.
"The next big arrival of coconut oil is expected on the first week of March with a cargo of 24,000 tonnes. We don't expect any big quantity for Rotterdam in April," said another trader.
Early this year, Philippine oil traders said they expected coconut oil exports in the country to increase starting in March or April on prospects of better crop harvests.
